subject: BrightPath Health — model fit & custom eval plan
messages:
From: Alexis Bongard <alexis.bongard@brightpathhealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Riley <tom.riley@brightpathhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: BrightPath discovery — next steps on evals

Thanks again for the intro call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can get the evaluation work started: 

- Use case: clinical triage suggestion + short summary for intake notes (single-turn + short context). Typical inputs are ~120-300 tokens.
- Primary goals: high factual accuracy on triage label, minimal hallucination in summary, runtime latency <200ms p50 in production.
- Data: we can provide ~2,500 de-identified historical cases in CSV/JSONL. Some records include free text with abbreviations.

As next steps, could you:
1) propose a short model shortlist and recommended evaluation metrics,
2) share an example prompt set and the expected dataset format for Redwood's eval harness, and
3) confirm any constraints around PII/de-identified data and whether we can run this in your hosted environment or need VPC/on-prem?

Tom and I are aiming to have a small pilot run within 2 weeks if possible. Thanks — Alexis

--
Alexis Bongard
Head of Clinical Ops | BrightPath Health
alexis.bongard@brightpathhealth.com
+1 415-555-0198
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Alexis Bongard <alexis.bongard@brightpathhealth.com>, Tom Riley <tom.riley@brightpathhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 12:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: BrightPath discovery — next steps on evals

Thanks Alexis — great conversation. Below is a concise post-call plan, recommended models, and the minimal artifacts we'd need to run a BrightPath-specific eval on Redwood. I copied Marissa to lead onboarding and Ben for commercial touchpoints.

Post-call summary (1 line): objective is a scoring + summary task — measure triage-label accuracy and summary faithfulness across a 2.5k record pilot.

Model shortlist (initial candidates):
- redwood-7b-instruct-qlora (good cost / latency balance)
- llama-2-13b-chat-q4f16 (strong instruction-following baseline)
- vicuna-13b-v1.5 (higher quality for free-text summarization; higher cost)
Notes: we'll run 1-2 variants (quantized vs FP16) and surface token/latency tradeoffs in the report.

Benchmark & evaluation artifacts (we will add to Drive and link in HubSpot):
- Prompt set (attached stub: brightpath_prompt_set_v1.jsonl) — short templates for triage classification and for summary generation.
- Benchmark template (attached: brightpath_benchmark_template.csv) — expected input columns and gold-reference structure.
- Redwood eval runbook (attached: redwood_eval_runbook.md) — how we execute runs and what we deliver.

Dataset format (minimal): newline-delimited JSON (".jsonl") with these string fields per line: 
- id: unique id (string)
- context: patient intake free text (string)
- question: instruction/prompt slot (string, use our prompt templates)
- gold_triage: canonical triage label (string)
- gold_summary: canonical short summary (string)
- metadata: optional free-form string (e.g., department, date bucket)
Example line: {"id":"bp-0001","context":"52M cough, fever 2d...","question":"Provide triage and 1-sentence summary.","gold_triage":"urgent","gold_summary":"Symptoms suggest likely bronchitis; recommend urgent clinician review.","metadata":"dept:teletriage"}

Scoring rubric (summary):
- Triage accuracy: micro accuracy (exact label match) and top-2 recall (if multi-label).
- Summary quality: 0-2 scale per sample (0 = incorrect/misleading, 1 = partially correct, 2 = correct & concise).
- Hallucination flag: binary per sample (1 if invented facts not present in context).
- Safety/PHI checks: binary flags (we run regex + heuristics, you can provide terms to redact).
- Aggregate: final score = weighted (0.6 triage accuracy + 0.3 mean summary score + 0.1 hallucination penalty) — we can adjust weights after alignment.

Run config for Redwood (recommended starter):
- model: redwood-7b-instruct-qlora / llama-2-13b-chat-q4f16
- temperature: 0.0 for triage, 0.2 for summary generation
- max_tokens: 256
- batch_size: 32 (we'll tune for latency SLOs)
- streaming: off for scoring runs

Deliverables and timeline (2-week pilot suggestion):
- Day 0-2: dataset transfer + schema validation (BrightPath to upload to Drive/S3)
- Day 3-5: prompt tuning & dry run on 100 samples (we supply 2 prompt variants)
- Day 6-9: full 2.5k runs across 2 models/variants
- Day 10-12: scoring, regression checks, and short report with latency/cost numbers + scorer CSV
- Day 13-14: review call and next-step proposal

Action items (owners):
- BrightPath: upload de-identified JSONL + confirm labels (Alexis)
- Redwood: Marissa to set up eval pipeline and share Drive link (Marissa)
- Redwood: Ben to confirm commercial terms for the pilot if we need reserved capacity (Ben)

Attachments included as stubs: brightpath_prompt_set_v1.jsonl, brightpath_benchmark_template.csv, redwood_eval_runbook.md

If that plan looks good, we'll kick off as soon as you upload the dataset. Happy to jump on a 30m follow-up tomorrow afternoon to walk through the prompt set.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123
From: Tom Riley <tom.riley@brightpathhealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Alexis Bongard <alexis.bongard@brightpathhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 14:00:00 -0400
Subject: Re: BrightPath discovery — next steps on evals

Thanks Aditya — this is helpful. A few clarifying Qs before we upload: 
1) PII/PHI: our security team wants confirmation that de-identification is sufficient for hosted runs. If not, we need to run the evals inside our AWS account / VPC. Do you support that for short pilots?
2) SOC2 / evidence: can you share the SOC2 Type II and indicate whether your eval pipeline writes logs with tenant IDs?
3) For the scoring rubric: can you confirm whether the hallucination detection is manual or automated? We need to understand how many samples will be manually reviewed.

Appreciate the timing and we'll aim to have the dataset uploaded by EOD Monday if the hosting piece is squared away.

—Tom
Tom Riley
VP Product | BrightPath Health
 tom.riley@brightpathhealth.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Tom Riley <tom.riley@brightpathhealth.com>, Alexis Bongard <alexis.bongard@brightpathhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 14:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: BrightPath discovery — next steps on evals

Tom — great questions. Short answers below and then an action proposal.

1) PII/PHI: Hosted runs are allowed if the data is de-identified to your standard (we run regex-based PHI checks during ingestion). If BrightPath requires, we can run the pilot inside your AWS account via our Redwood Private VPC connector (we've done this for pilots; Marissa will coordinate).

2) SOC2 / evidence: Redwood has a SOC2 Type II report; link here: https://redwood.ai/soc2-report.pdf. Our eval pipeline emits audit logs with tenant IDs and run IDs; logs can be forwarded to your SIEM or stored in your S3 bucket when using the VPC connector.

3) Hallucination detection: automated heuristics for initial flagging (entity mismatch + factual overlap) and a small manual adjudication sample (we typically sample 5-10% for manual review; we can change that). We'll include a CSV with automated flags + a column for manual adjudicator notes if you want to scale manual review.

Action proposal:
- If you are comfortable with de-identified hosted runs, upload to the Drive link and we'll start schema validation immediately.
- If you prefer the VPC connector, Marissa will send an onboarding checklist and a short network config template today.

Marissa — can you: 1) create the eval project in Redwood for BrightPath, 2) share the Drive/S3 upload link and template, 3) estimate the cost and wall-clock run time for 2.5k samples across 2 models (ballpark)?

Ben — please prepare a pilot quote; we can keep it informal until BrightPath requests a PO.

Alexis/Tom — I'll hold a 30m slot tomorrow at 3pm ET to walk the prompt set if that works — otherwise suggest a time.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

Aditya Rao
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
